faq: Will site owners have to reinstall the app?
No. We keep your app ID and settings, so installed apps update in place. If a new permission is needed, we plan how owners approve it and write the notice.
What if my app uses Velo code?
We include it. Velo code and collections are mapped like the rest. We note anything that must change because of newer SDK rules, and move it in the same package where it fits.
What happens to my existing data?
It stays. We map every collection and field first, move it with a tested script and verify counts on a copy before the real update. The Premium package adds a backup and a restore test.
Is there downtime during the move?
Usually none. We build and test on a copy, then release at a time you choose. If a data move needs a short pause, we say so in the rollout notes in advance.
desc:
Wix app migration moves an older app to the latest Wix app framework and current APIs without losing your users. Ecom Swift LLC lists what the app depends on, rebuilds it with the Wix CLI, moves stored data safely and tests every step.

## What is a Wix app migration?

A Wix app migration is the process of moving an app built on older Wix tooling or deprecated APIs onto the current framework. The work covers rebuilding dashboard pages and site widgets, replacing outdated API calls, moving stored data into a structure the new code can read and checking that billing and plans still work. The aim is for site owners to keep using the app, with no visible break.

## Why older Wix apps eventually need to move

Platforms retire tools. An app built several framework generations ago may still run today, but each year it depends on more things Wix has stopped developing. New features, new editor behavior and new dashboard components are built for the current framework, so the older app falls further behind.

Waiting makes the move harder. The longer old code stays, the more developers who understood it leave, and the more owners depend on it. A planned migration done while the app still works is far safer than an emergency rewrite after something stops.

## How migration affects your app's future

A migrated app can use current Wix capabilities, pass current App Market checks and be maintained by any developer familiar with the Wix CLI. Widgets behave the way the modern editor expects, and the dashboard fits the Wix Design System.

The most important result is continuity. Site owners should not need to reconfigure anything, and their records should still be there. Whether a particular old feature has an exact modern equivalent depends on what Wix offers at the time, so we confirm each item before we start rather than assume.

## What a careful migration includes

- A report of deprecated APIs and components in use.
- A map of every page, widget and backend function.
- Rebuilt pages and widgets on the current Wix CLI framework.
- Updated API calls, each tested after the change.
- A plan for moving data collections, with a backup taken first.
- Dashboard pages rebuilt with the Wix Design System.
- A check of billing, plans and subscription handling.
- Install and update tests on development sites, including an update from the old version.
- A rollout plan for existing site owners.
- Notes on any behavior that has to change, so you can tell users in advance.

## How we carry it out

We begin with an inventory, because surprises in old code cause the most delay. Then we agree the order of work, often starting with the part that is easiest to isolate. We rebuild on a copy, never directly on the live app, and test each step on a development site.

The Basic package covers the report and the move of one widget or page. Standard moves a small app in full, with data mapped and kept and an update test for existing installs. Premium covers a complete migration with backup and restore tests, billing checks, a rollout plan and a period of bug fixes. If your app contains Velo code, we review it and move what the new framework supports.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Back up every data collection before the work starts.
- Tell us which features your site owners use most.
- Pick a quiet time for the final release.
- Warn site owners in advance if anything will look different.

**Avoid:**
- Moving everything at once with no way back.
- Editing the live app while the migration is in progress.
- Skipping the update test from the old version.
- Assuming old and new data structures match without checking.

## Who this is for

An owner of a long-running app built on tools Wix no longer promotes. A company that inherited an app with unclear code. A team that wants new features but cannot add them to the old base.

## What we need from you

Repository access, collaborator access to your Dev Center and a list of known quirks. We never need your password. If you have documentation or notes from the original developer, send them, since they save time during the inventory.
